title: Collision Prediction for Robotics Accelerators
problem: Motion planning in dynamic environments requires expensive collision detection queries to validate candidate paths. Currently, 25%-41% of these queries could be eliminated if collision outcomes could be predicted before detailed computation.
motivation: Real-time collision detection is a critical bottleneck in autonomous robotics systems that must evaluate multiple candidate paths continuously.
method: COORD predicts collision outcomes by exploiting spatial locality of robot poses using simple hashing and saturating counters. A hardware collision prediction unit (COPU) is integrated with existing collision detection accelerators to prefilter queries, prioritizing evaluation of predicted collisions and eliminating safe poses from detailed detection.
key_novelty: Using spatial locality patterns with simple hashing mechanisms to predict collision outcomes and eliminate 25-41% of collision detection queries before expensive computation.
contributions: Observation that 25%-41% of collision detection queries can be predicted as unsafe and eliminated
COORD mechanism leveraging spatial locality with hashing and saturating counters for collision prediction
COPU hardware collision prediction unit integrated with collision detection accelerators
17.2%-32.1% reduction in collision detection queries and 1.23× performance/watt improvement on neural motion planners
primary_theme: collision prediction for accelerated robotics motion planning
